why: Compare from both ends inside each block: a block of length k is a palindrome when position i matches position k-1-i, and each mismatched mirror pair costs exactly one change. So walk two pointers inward through each block and count mismatches.
hints: Blocks are independent. For one block, which pairs of positions must be equal?
Mirror pairs (i, k-1-i). A pair that differs needs exactly one change (set either side to the other); a matching pair needs none.
For each block start b, walk lo = b, hi = b+k-1 inward and count s[lo] != s[hi]. O(n) total.
pitfalls: k = 1: every block is already a palindrome, answer 0.
The middle character of an odd block never needs a change.
Count pairs, not characters: one change fixes a mismatched pair.
